headlines.text: Iranian attack on Saudi tanker killed two Filipino sailors, Saudi Arabia says. The kingdom condemns the targeting of Sidr, which was reportedly hit by unknown projectiles in the Strait of Hormuz on Monday.
Protests in Spain over government's handling of Ceuta migrant crisis. Spanish opposition parties accuse Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez of abandoning the residents of Ceuta.

EU and Nato vow to step up pressure on Russia after 'new escalation' in Germany. Russia is accused of growing increasingly reckless after Berlin blamed Russia for a failed drone attack on Leipzig airport.
Rosenberg: Putin's veiled threat to UK part of Russia's campaign against West. The Russian president wants to keep Britain guessing - and stressing - over Moscow's real intentions.
Watch: Jury still unable to reach unanimous decision in Lindsay Clancy case. For a second time in two days, jurors told the judge they could not agree on a verdict in the murder trial.
Maltese tycoon acquitted of orchestrating murder of renowned journalist. Daphne Caruana Galizia exposed corruption and money laundering schemes in Malta before she was killed by a car bomb in 2017.

Netherlands moves billions in gold to London in 'crisis preparedness' move. The Dutch central bank removes some of its gold reserves from the US and Canada, saying it is because of "increasing geopolitical unrest".

Iran says US strike killed four at wedding in 'war crime' as US denies targeting civilians. Iranian media reports two children were among those killed when shrapnel hit a home. Iran then launched missiles and drones at US targets in the Middle East.
US sailors arrive in Thailand's Pattaya after record 250 days at sea. The USS Abraham Lincoln is docking close to Pattaya, known for its neon-lit nightlife, and for sex tourism.
Uber shuts operations in Nigeria and Uganda with immediate effect. Nigeria - Africa's most populous country - is proving a tough market for ride-hailing services.
Woman charged with juror intimidation in Lindsay Clancy trial. Dawn Light is accused of taking photos of jurors outside the Plymouth courthouse, a practice prohibited by the court.

Zelensky says airlines should avoid Russian airspace as Ukraine escalates drone operations. Chinese and Gulf state airlines are among those still using Russian airspace. Meanwhile, Russia says it will intensify its own attacks on Ukraine.

More than 900 killed in Gaza this year despite ceasefire, Hamas-run health ministry says. The ministry says the total number of people killed in the Strip since 10 October is now more than 1,300, including 301 children.
South African airline behind daring stadium stunt cancels next flyby. The civil aviation authority says it is also investigating last Saturday's aerial display.
Ariana Grande makes emotional tour exit and steps back from public life. The star makes an emotional farewell as she wraps up a tour she's described as her "last hurrah".

Facilitating AI integration with simplicity at scale. As companies scale, the technology supporting operations can become a liability just as quickly as it becomes an asset. Disconnected systems, site-specific tools, spreadsheets, and manual workarounds can create data silos that make it harder to spot problems early, coordinate responses, and make decisions with confiden

The Download: AI puzzles and a path to our nearest star system. This is today’s edition of The Download, our weekday newsletter that provides a daily dose of what’s going on in the world of technology. AI models flub these intelligence tests. Can you fare any better? Puzzles and games have always been central to AI development. The term “machine learning” was popularize

Pentagon orders mandatory testosterone tests for male troops 30 and older. The Pentagon's new mandatory testosterone deficiency screening for troops ages 30 and up includes mandatory blood tests and voluntary hormone replacement therapy for men.

Social media is Lindsay Clancy wild card that could tilt potential retrial to the defense, retired judge says. Lindsay Clancy's deadlocked jury received a Tuey-Rodriguez charge as a retired judge warns social media could give her defense an edge in a retrial.

US military boards, searches and sinks vessel allegedly supporting Los Choneros narco-terrorists. Video captures USS San Antonio Marines boarding and sinking a Los Choneros narco-terrorist floating refueling station in the Eastern Pacific.

15-year-old accused of firing into crowd during deadly Seattle mass shooting claims self-defense. A 15-year-old claims self-defense in the deadly Bite of Seattle shootout, but prosecutors say he recklessly fired a ghost gun into a packed crowd.

Rams legend Eric Dickerson speaks on Los Angeles Angels sale, says new owner Stan Kroenke 'likes winning'. Eric Dickerson praised Stan Kroenke as a winner while throwing the first pitch at Angel Stadium amid the Angels' $4 billion ownership change.

Federal judge dismisses DOJ lawsuit challenging California policy allowing biological males in girls’ sports. A federal judge dismissed the Department of Justice lawsuit against California over transgender athletes competing in girls' sports on procedural grounds.

Maine's high court gives father final say over daughter’s church attendance. The Maine Supreme Judicial Court upheld a father's authority over his daughter's attendance at an evangelical church after a pastor singled him out by name.

Rory McIlroy admits he's not interested in playing most PGA Tour events moving forward. Rory McIlroy admitted at the Tour Championship that his playing schedule is shrinking, saying his fuse is shorter after 18 years as a professional.

FAA seeks permanent airspace restrictions near Trump’s Mar-a-Lago as expert warns rules are ‘not good enough’. The FAA proposed permanent flight rules near Donald J. Trump International Airport at Secret Service request, but drone expert warns it's may not be enough.
Tim Curry's cause of death revealed. Tim Curry died from coronary artery disease, with stroke and kidney cancer listed as contributing factors, according to public health documents.

'I mean, clearly,' Jalen Hurts tells GQ when asked if he and A.J. Brown grew apart in Philadelphia. Jalen Hurts confirmed to GQ that he and A.J. Brown "clearly" grew apart before the wide receiver was traded to the New England Patriots in June.

Justin Tucker looks to make NFL comeback after spa allegations, works out with the Jets. Justin Tucker worked out for the New York Jets alongside two other kickers, marking another attempt at an NFL comeback amid unresolved questions.

'We need to return immediately,' flight crew warns as pilot health emergency unfolds. Air traffic control audio captured the urgent moment a Delta Air Lines crew declared a potential pilot incapacitation minutes after takeoff and asked to return to the airport.

'Wheel of Fortune' announcer Jim Thornton's attorney speaks out after game show suspension. Jim Thornton's lawyer says the "Wheel of Fortune" announcer was not arrested or charged after a passenger complained on an American Airlines flight.
The primary is over; now come the primetime mistakes. Not every candidate is Deion Sanders in Primetime. Abdul El-Sayed and Darline Graham face questions about whether they're ready for the Senate.

Ex-Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro and wife seek to end drug charges case on immunity grounds. Former Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro and his wife have asked a judge to dismiss the drug trafficking indictment against them on the grounds that they have immunity as the leader and first lady of a foreign country

NBA suspends Clippers owner Ballmer, fines team $30M, Kawhi Leonard $700K in cap circumvention case. Los Angeles Clippers owner Steve Ballmer was suspended for one year by the NBA, and the team was ordered to pay $30 million for violating salary cap circumvention rules in a case involving Kawhi Leonard.

The IRS slashed its staff. One result? More taxes going uncollected. The IRS slashed its auditing staff last year — but the move may have backfired as tax collections from enforcement efforts plummeted, an Inspector General report shows.

A jury in Malta acquits a businessman in the killing of reporter Daphne Caruana Galizia. Investigative journalist Daphne Caruana Galizia had written extensively about suspected corruption in political and business circles in Malta. She was killed by a car bomb in 2017, at age 53.

New Jersey asks Supreme Court to resolve fight over Kalshi's future. If the high court accepts the petition, it would tee up a case with sweeping implications for prediction markets, an industry that has unleashed billions of dollars of betting across nearly every aspect of modern life.

New immigration court tactic leads to huge lines and chaos in Miami. Chaos unfolds at the Miami immigration court after judges are assigned mega master calendars, hearings where judges see more than 100 immigrants at once.

Understanding the tech giants' oversized influence in American schools. Big tech companies like Apple and Microsoft use devices, training and conferences for teachers and students to embed in schools. The New York Times' Natasha Singer discusses the impact in Coding Kids.

Iran fires on its Gulf neighbors, retaliating for U.S. strikes after a monthlong lull. The six-month war has led to a spike in oil prices, roiled the global economy and posed increasing political problems for President Trump's Republican Party ahead of November midterm elections.

Greetings from the Royal Pavilion, a stunning reminder of India in southern England. Looking up at this 18th century building, it became clear the British didn't only bring their architectural style to India. They also took some of India's style home.

Chevron to expand in Venezuela, days after the U.S. and Venezuela strike oil deal. Chevron is the largest foreign oil operator in Venezuela. The deal will expand its footprint at a time of political and economic uncertainty for Venezuela.
Kuwait fends off Iranian attack as Trump says renewed Mideast hostilities will not last 'too long'. On Thursday, Kuwait's army said it was confronting hostile missile and drone attacks from Iran.

Trump and Xi are set to meet in DC. Why some China watchers have low expectations. Trump's summit with Xi is expected to take place less than six weeks before the U.S. election, with polls showing Democrats favored to make gains in Congress.

South Korea's semiconductor exports just tripled year-over-year. Is it too much of a good thing?. If growth were to slow in the semiconductor sector, would the slowdown take the Korean economy with it?

CNBC Daily Open: U.S.-China meeting in focus while Trump wants to rename the Strait of Hormuz. All eyes are on the upcoming meeting between U.S. President Donald Trump and Chinese leader Xi Jinping at the White House, which could offer more clues to the U.S.-China trade relations as well as China's stance towards Iran amid the Mideast conflict.

Inside India newsletter: India’s economic growth is smashing forecasts, but its biggest stocks aren't feeling the love. India's strong economic growth has surprised every quarter for the last year, but the performance of its key stock benchmarks has been deeply disappointing.
Global bond rout gathers pace as inflation fears mount. Borrowing costs continue to extend multi-decade highs as nerves over inflation, higher rates and high debt remain at the fore.
USTR's Greer huddles with House Republicans amid Trump trade spats. Trump's plan to lower tariffs on 300,000 metric tons of imported beef caused an uproar among cattle ranchers.

Energy Secretary Chris Wright tells CNBC more than 17 million barrels of oil transited Hormuz on Monday. The Energy secretary spoke to CNBC's Brian Sullivan in Venezuela on Wednesday, after President Donald Trump announced a massive oil deal with Caracas.
Why Hilton calls this Asian country the fastest-growing tourism market. Hilton says one Asian country is the most exciting global tourism market as regional travel surges.

Scaramucci says he had 'Potomac fever' in the White House — and Bessent and Lutnick have it too. "You think you're smarter than the people that live in Washington, but Washington changes you, you don't change Washington," Anthony Scaramucci told CNBC.

China's Xi keeps Iranian president at arm's length weeks ahead of Trump summit. China's Xi gave Iran's Pezeshkian a brief, low-profile audience at the SCO summit, as Beijing seeks to avoid appearing close to Tehran ahead of a high-stakes summit with Trump.

The $3 trillion oil market is becoming more accessible than ever: No longer a 'rich man's game'. Oil trading is becoming more accessible to individual investors as smaller futures contracts, ETFs and online brokerages lower longtime barriers to the market.

States now must report undocumented immigrants to DHS or risk federal funding, DOJ says. The new DOJ opinion relates to funding states get for Temporary Assistance for Needy Families and the Supplemental Security Income programs.

NBA suspends Clippers owner Ballmer for one year in Kawhi Leonard salary cap probe. The NBA also fined the Los Angeles Clippers $30 million and said the team will forfeit five first-round picks, one in each year in drafts starting in 2029.

Berkshire CEO Greg Abel says Japanese bond yields not a challenge for trading houses right now. In an appearance on CNBC's "Squawk Box," Greg Abel said that yields in the country are still relatively low.
